Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Initial discovery — access models, KMS, and connectivity (RegulaHealth)

Hi Lena —

Thanks for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please correct anything I get wrong.

Key pain points you shared:
- Strict data residency and audit requirements for patient PII (FIPS/KMS-backed keys, per-environment key separation).
- Limited trust zone: production model inference must run in RegulaHealth-controlled VPC or air-gapped on-prem cluster for certain clinical workflows.
- Network constraints: egress to public internet is highly restricted; only approved endpoints via a proxy are allowed.
- Performance targets: 99th percentile inference latency <= 350ms for short clinical prompts (<=512 tokens).

Current stack and constraints:
- Primary app: RegulaHealth EHR augmentation service (on-prem primary, AWS staging).
- Identity: Okta SSO; they manage user identities and service accounts.
- Key management: Internal HSM (Thales) for production keys.
- Security team requires SOC2 + HITRUST alignment and a vendor security questionnaire.

Success criteria you outlined:
1) Proof that Redwood Private can be deployed inside RegulaHealth VPC with customer-managed KMS (separate keys per environment).
2) Network plan showing required egress/inbound ports and optional proxy support for model updates.
3) An audit artifact demonstrating access logs and key usage for 30-day retention.
4) Performance validation with a small pilot (10k requests/day) meeting latency SLO.

Immediate next steps (we suggested):
- I will share a short on‑prem/VPC primer and a sample KMS integration playbook (attached).
- You to share your vendor security questionnaire and any initial SOC/HITRUST evidence that would help us scope compliance work.
- Schedule a technical workshop with your infra and SecOps teams next week to walk through network flow and key rotation.

Can you confirm availability for a 60-minute workshop on Thu 14 Jan or Fri 15 Jan (morning PT)? Also, please loop in the procurement address for contract/SLAs discussions once we have scope.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_primer.pdf (pdf), reg_round1_requirements.csv (csv, referenced)

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Initial discovery — access models, KMS, and connectivity (RegulaHealth)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches my notes and is a helpful framing. A few clarifications and answers below.

Clarifications:
- The HSM is our canonical key store for PHI encryption at rest; RegulaHealth policy requires that vendor services either use our CMK (via external key control) or run entirely inside our trust boundary.
- For the initial pilot, the scope is limited to non-production clinical search augmentation (so we can test real load without touching live PHI); however, the long-term expectation is to enable production flows once controls are validated.
- Network: outbound-only egress is permissible but only to allowlisted IPs; we do have an approved proxy that can be used for software updates and model pulls.

Requested items we will send:
- Vendor security questionnaire (attached as Regula_Vendor_Q_SecuredOps.xlsx) — SecOps is copying in to validate answers.
- Our procurement team (procurement@regulahealth.com) is on the thread for early contract questions.

Availability: Thu 14 Jan 09:30–11:30 PT works for my infra and SecOps leads. If that slot still works for you and your engineers, please lock it.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Lead Product Manager, Clinical AI | RegulaHealth
Lena.ortiz@regulahealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0247
